full_judgment:
8. Mr Ahmed Nawshed Jamil, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-petitioner in the course of his arguments after placing the judgment of both the Courts below as well as the evidence of PWs and DWs submits that the plaintiff has been owning and possessing the suit land by paying rent and taxes to the Government which is apparent form 2 decrees passed in Other Class Suit No. 476 of 1983 and 479 of 1983 although the Court of appeal below without adverting this vital aspects of the case ignoring the decrees passed in Other Class Suit No. 476 of 1983 and 479 of 1983 most illegally set-aside the well founded judgment of the trial Court below. The learned Advocate further submits that defendants have no legal basis as to claim of the suit land, the decrees passed in Other Class Suit No. 476 of 1983 and 479 of 1983 are still alive and, as such, the impugned judgment of the appellate Court below is not a proper judgment of reversal which is liable to be set-aside. 

 23. In view of the discussions above, I find no difficulty whatever in holding that the impugned judgment is not a proper judgment of reversal, which does not deserve to be sustained. The contentions raised by the learned Advocate for the defendant opposite parties for the aforesaid reasons are of no substance. The decision cited by the learned Advocate for the opposite parties is distinguishable on facts.
